name: Glassjaw
label: Warner Bros.
lede: Two kids from a Long Island summer camp who made a post-hardcore blueprint, told fans to pirate it to spite their own label, sold 7-inches you couldn't play without a plastic logo, and took fifteen years to make a third album.

eras.title: Two kids from summer camp
eras.text: Daryl Palumbo and Justin Beck met at camp and grew up on New York hardcore: Youth of Today, Bad Brains, Sick of It All. Glassjaw spent six years cycling through members on Long Island before a producer heard a demo and lost his mind.

years.h: Daryl Palumbo and Justin Beck start Glassjaw
years.p: The two met at summer camp. Beck said Swiftkick was the name he liked first, but Glassjaw stuck, after early versions spelled xGlassjawx and The Glassjaw.

years.h: Glassjaw's first show, in Oceanside, New York
years.p: Glassjaw plays its first show in Oceanside on Long Island's South Shore, near Palumbo's hometown of Bellmore.

years.h: Daryl Palumbo is diagnosed with Crohn's disease
years.p: The illness will shape Glassjaw for decades: it becomes the subject of the title track of the first album and the reason for years of canceled tours.

years.h: Kiss Kiss Bang Bang EP on 2 Cents a Pop
years.p: Five songs from Palumbo, Beck, Todd Weinstock, Kris Baldwin and Ariel Telford. Star Above My Bed is still in Glassjaw's setlists decades later.

years.h: Justin Beck moves from drums to bass to guitar
years.p: Beck started on drums, switched to bass when Ariel Telford left in 1998, and moves to guitar when Kris Baldwin leaves and Manuel Carrero joins on bass.

years.h: Ross Robinson hears the demo and wants in
years.p: Producer [[Ross Robinson|df05fc2e-6ff2-4ba1-95b3-ccb7ede14691]] finds Glassjaw's demo and talks Roadrunner Records into signing them. Justin Beck remembers him jumping up at practice, shouting that he'd do it.

eras.title: A war with Roadrunner
eras.text: The debut made Glassjaw a name, and the label that released it became their enemy. By the end of 2001 the band was telling fans to steal its own record.

q: You don't talk to a woman like that. It's offensive.
years.h: Everything You Ever Wanted to Know About Silence
years.p: Made over two months at Indigo Ranch in Malibu with Ross Robinson, [[Sammy Siegler|869c662b-574c-46ac-acf6-3dc6f025fd5a]] of [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]] on drums. NME compared it to Jeff Buckley doused in napalm.
years.xp:
Robinson said the mission was to take down the Adidas rock of nu-metal bands like Limp Bizkit. The songs are mostly about relationship pain, and the album drew criticism for misogyny. Palumbo later agreed.

It reached No. 82 in the UK and, according to Wikipedia, sold over 47,000 copies in the U.S.
play: Everything You Ever Wanted to Know About Silence

years.h: Six weeks in Europe with Deftones and Soulfly
years.p: Glassjaw tours Europe behind [[Deftones|7527f6c2-d762-4b88-b5e2-9244f1e34c46]] and [[Soulfly|832a43c7-aa7d-439b-a6b4-4f1afa671c24]]. Larry Gorman of [[Orange 9mm|66ae7e89-680b-4f0f-a990-8a4e0bdf3d51]] takes over as the band's drummer on the road.

years.big: Don't buy our record. Steal it.
q: Our goal at the time of that record was to destroy Adidas rock
years.h: Glassjaw leaves Roadrunner and tells fans to download
years.p: Glassjaw says Roadrunner barely promoted the album and wouldn't let Daryl Palumbo rest when Crohn's disease flared on tour. They quit the label and urge fans to download the album illegally.
years.xp:
Palumbo called Roadrunner a joke and the scourge of the music industry; Justin Beck told fans never to support anything from the label. Robinson said the band's goal was plain.

Meanwhile Glassjaw had already recorded its second album in secret with Robinson.

eras.title: Worship and Tribute, and a hospital in Paris
eras.text: On Warner Bros., Glassjaw made its most admired record and then couldn't tour it: Palumbo's Crohn's disease put him in hospitals in Paris and Glasgow. By 2004 the band's website read RIP.

years.h: Worship and Tribute on Warner Bros.
years.p: Produced by Ross Robinson with [[Shannon Larkin|736a6ab6-1b97-4b5f-a36e-dc7e295e8715]] of [[Godsmack|ac2d1c91-3667-46aa-9fe7-170ca7fce9e2]] drumming. It hits No. 82 on the Billboard 200, Glassjaw's only entry there, and Pitchfork later calls it genre-defining.
years.xp: September 11 happened while the songs were being written and colored the record. The song Convectuoso was held back because Roadrunner claimed it, and only came home on the 2022 vinyl reissue. Singles: Cosmopolitan Bloodloss and Ape Dos Mil.

years.h: Warped Tour, Ozzfest and a new bassist
years.p: Glassjaw works the big summer tours, Warped and Ozzfest, plus Snocore, with Dave Allen now on bass.

years.h: Daryl Palumbo hospitalized in Paris, tour canceled
years.p: A Crohn's relapse puts Palumbo in a Paris hospital for intestinal surgery, wiping out Glassjaw's German and UK dates. He relapses again in December.

years.h: A Glasgow hospital, and London canceled again
years.p: Palumbo is hospitalized in Glasgow. Glassjaw cancels more shows, including the Kerrang! Weekender and the London Astoria.

years.h: Palumbo's pop side band [[Head Automatica|5e94030f-c3c7-4777-a5af-5ecfbfc37bba]]
years.p: Palumbo releases Decadence with Head Automatica, Larry Gorman drumming, while Justin Beck builds his merchandise company.

years.h: Three members fired; the website says RIP Glassjaw
years.p: Guitarist Todd Weinstock, bassist Dave Allen and drummer Larry Gorman are fired. The band denies it has split and points to Palumbo's Crohn's disease.

eras.title: 100% maybe
eras.text: Glassjaw came back as a four-piece, played rarely, and spent years recording an album nobody heard. When Warner Bros. restructured, the band walked with its tapes.

years.h: Manuel Carrero and Durijah Lang lock in
years.p: Glassjaw plays three shows, including a charity benefit in Farmingdale and a spot with [[The Used|8262d8e4-9137-4bb3-a787-3caabbbc13e9]] at Hammerstein Ballroom. Carrero returns on bass and Lang takes the drums; nobody replaces Weinstock.

years.h: El Mark EP: B-sides from Worship and Tribute
years.p: Glassjaw's first release in three years is leftovers from the Warner Bros. album.

years.h: On tour with Deftones, and the Fucking Tour 2006
years.p: Glassjaw supports Deftones and headlines a run of its own, then plays New Year's Eve with [[Hatebreed|40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2]] at Connecticut's Stillborn Fest.

years.h: Brixton: Glassjaw's first UK show in four years
years.p: Glassjaw headlines the Carling Academy Brixton, and later calls its Southern California run the 100% Maybe tour.

years.h: Thirteen songs recorded, vocals pending
years.p: Justin Beck, producing with engineer Jonathan Florencio, has drums, bass and guitar done for thirteen songs, including Jesus Glue and a reworked Star Above My Bed.

years.h: Glassjaw and Warner Bros. part ways
years.p: Glassjaw leaves Warner after corporate restructuring and a dispute over Palumbo's shelved Head Automatica album Swan Damage. The band keeps its recordings.

years.h: Carrero and Lang quit Saves the Day for Glassjaw
years.p: Manuel Carrero and Durijah Lang leave [[Saves the Day|593f8594-83ad-4df4-a9b8-e4d225f55440]] to make Glassjaw their only band.

eras.title: The biggest DIY band in the world
eras.text: Free of labels, Glassjaw sold its new songs through Justin Beck's merch company, on dates that matched their titles, and Rock Sound crowned it the biggest DIY band in the world. Then the rhythm section left.

years.cap: The die-cut logo you needed to play it
years.h: A 7-inch you can't play without the plastic logo
years.p: On 8/8 at Hevy Fest, Glassjaw sells All Good Junkies Go to Heaven on spray-painted vinyl that needs a die-cut plastic logo to play. It sells out in hours.
years.xp: Jesus Glue followed on 9/9, Natural Born Farmer on 10/10 and You Think You're (John Fucking Lennon) on 12/12, which sold out instantly. Buying merch got you the songs as free downloads.

years.h: Our Color Green (The Singles) goes digital
years.p: The 2010 vinyl singles are collected into one EP and released to iTunes, Amazon and eMusic.

years.h: Coloring Book: an EP handed out free at shows
years.p: After the first concert of the tour, Glassjaw gives the new EP away to everyone at the venue. The song Gold streamed first, at 11:11 a.m. on January 11.

years.h: Worship and Tribute in full at Irving Plaza
years.p: When Sonisphere is canceled, Glassjaw books Irving Plaza in New York and plays its 2002 album start to finish.

years.h: Manuel Carrero and Durijah Lang quit
years.p: The rhythm section leaves after a decade, later joining the reunited [[Burn|502429d5-da95-4a78-bfc9-7c8cf93504e6]]. Lang said he had no axe to grind and just ran out of reasons not to call it a day.

years.h: Surprise show at Amityville Music Hall
years.p: Glassjaw debuts bassist Travis Sykes and drummer Chad Hasty, both from Glass Cloud, at a surprise Long Island show.

years.h: Opening for [[Coheed and Cambria|ae1b47d5-5128-431c-9d30-e08fd90e0767]], playing unreleased songs
years.p: Glassjaw supports Coheed and Cambria in the UK and U.S. and plays small headline shows full of new material. In December, [[Billy Rymer|b6587c65-10ca-4c64-bc37-dd02f7ce7a72]] of The Dillinger Escape Plan says he tracked a whole album of drums.

eras.title: Material Control, fifteen years on
eras.text: Glassjaw's third album arrived via an Amazon leak, fifteen years after the second. The band that never breaks up spent the following years playing its old records for their anniversaries.

years.h: Material Control, the first album in fifteen years
years.p: An Amazon listing leaks the album two weeks early; Century Media releases it December 1. Fans who had bought from Justin Beck's MerchDirect got a ten-song flexi-disc.
years.xp: Billy Rymer plays drums on the record. It reached No. 7 on the U.S. Independent chart and No. 12 on the Rock chart. Videos for Shira and Golgotha followed in 2018.

years.h: Co-headlining with [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]]
years.p: Glassjaw tours the U.S. with Walter Schreifels' Quicksand behind Material Control.

years.h: Twenty years of Worship and Tribute
years.p: Glassjaw plays anniversary shows for its first two albums, and the Worship and Tribute vinyl reissue finally includes Convectuoso.

years.h: Glassjaw on the Vans Warped Tour, again
years.p: Glassjaw is announced for the 2026 Warped Tour, 24 years after its Worship and Tribute summer on the same tour.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Everything You Ever Wanted to Know About Silence
